steps: 1. Download the article PDF file and the supplementary information PDF file with curl.

2. Run 'pdftotext -layout' on both PDF files. Also run plain 'pdftotext' on the supplementary file as a second reading of Supplementary Table 2, because that table interleaves four rankings across the page.
3. Fetch the publisher HTML version of Table 1 as a second reading of Table 1. The HTML and the PDF agree cell for cell.
4. Transcribe each of the eight rankings by hand into the Python script build_beck.py, reading from the layout text. Each ranking holds 15 or 30 rows.
5. Merge the eight rankings on a normalised country name with pandas. Write the CSV file.
extraction_method.manual_transcription_note: The eight rankings were typed by hand from the layout text, then checked against the layout text a second time and against the publisher HTML table for Table 1.

known_gaps: The paper publishes NO country table for the 10-year, 25-year or 50-year storm events. Supplementary Table 1 covers the 100-year event only. The article reports the 10, 25, 50 and 100 year results only as global figures in Figure 3 and Figure 4 and as global sentences in the text.

The paper publishes NO full per-country table. Only the top 15 or top 30 countries appear. The data availability statement says the data are 'mappable and downloadable at http://maps.oceanwealth.org/' and that the underlying data sets are 'available on request from IHCantabria'. The analyst did not test those two routes.
Supplementary Data 1 (file 41467_2018_4568_MOESM4_ESM.xlsx) holds a methods comparison table only, with no country data.
The unit of the column annual_averted_damages_over_gdp is not stated in the source.
